content: Celiac disease is observed to have a higher prevalence among youth diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, with rates ranging from approximately 1% to 16%. Screening for celiac disease should include testing for tissue transglutaminase IgA (tTG IgA) and total serum IgA levels. This screening is recommended at the time of type 1 diabetes diagnosis and should be repeated if symptoms suggestive of celiac disease arise or if there is a family history of the condition in first-degree relatives. For individuals diagnosed with celiac disease, adherence to a strict gluten-free diet is essential to alleviate symptoms and prevent potential complications associated with the condition. It is strongly advised that these individuals work closely with a registered dietitian who has expertise in managing both diabetes and celiac disease to ensure optimal dietary management and overall health outcomes.
